newsitem.title: CHINA: China bank chief hopes local currency decision soon.
newsitem.headline: China bank chief hopes local currency decision soon.

text.p: China central bank governor Dai Xianglong said the central government had decided to allow foreign banks to conduct local currency business in Shanghai and he hoped to make an announcement by the end of the year.

The governor of the People's Bank of China said he would like to go to Shanghai to disclose which banks would be selected, although he said he could not specify precisely when the announcement would be made.

"I can make it very clear to you that we have won the approval from the central government to allow foreign banks to conduct local currency business in Shanghai," Dai told Reuters in a recent interview.
"By winning approval we are authorised to let foreign banks do local currency business in the Pudong area (of Shanghai)," he said.
The statement was the clearest indication that Shanghai was still the site for the experimental permission for foreign banks to accept deposits and extend loans in renminbi, China's currency.
China has said for some time that it planned to allow foreign banks, which are now restricted to foreign currency business, into the domestic market on a limited basis.
Foreign banks have been keen to get a toehold in the local currency market as most Chinese companies have a greater demand for renminbi funding.

But Chinese banking industry sources say there is considerable opposition from domestic banks to letting big foreign financial institutions into the domestic market just as competition from new Chinese banks intensifies.
Other bankers and economists had said they heard little discussion of Shanghai as the site, suggesting that other cities might have been placed under consideration.
Dai's remarks also signalled that the central bank still did not have complete independence on such a sensitive issue and had to turn to political authorities for guidance.
"Personally, I hope to go to Shanghai by the end of this year to announce which foreign banks have been selected to do Chinese currency business," Dai said.
"I can't tell you the exact date for this announcement," he said.
The governor said a group of five to six banks could be selected first but that other groups would be chosen afterwards.
He did not give details of how they would be selected or when the subsequent groups would be announced.
The main business of the foreign banks would be taking institutional deposits and extending loans.
Foreign banks would be treated the same as domestic banks in terms of reserve requirements, Dai said.

A central bank spokesman said on Wednesday that one of the issues holding up implementation of the policy was the lack a regulatory framework. Detailed rules had to be formulated on issues that included taxation.
